3edafdb5-d174-547d-900a-fe3a9ebe3f2e.name: MemTier VM Allocated if Powered On (KB)
3edafdb5-d174-547d-900a-fe3a9ebe3f2e.description: Per VM: configured memory if running, zero if not. Exists to be rolled up; it is not interesting on a single VM.

c8545a57-91e1-57e2-9240-86fa875ae62f.name: MemTier Allocated Powered On (GB)
c8545a57-91e1-57e2-9240-86fa875ae62f.description: Allocated counting only powered-on VMs. THIS is the figure to size against. The plain Allocated beside it includes powered-off VMs and templates, which still report configured memory and are reclamation candidates, not demand.

669b5085-8f41-54e3-9a05-6dca4a21b6eb.name: MemTier Allocated Powered Off (GB)
669b5085-8f41-54e3-9a05-6dca4a21b6eb.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) / 1048576) - (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, attribute=Super Metric|sm_3edafdb5-d174-547d-900a-fe3a9ebe3f2e, depth=2}) / 1048576)
669b5085-8f41-54e3-9a05-6dca4a21b6eb.description: The gap between the two: memory configured to VMs that are not running, measured at 20.3% of allocated on one estate. A reclamation opportunity, and a warning that anything derived from plain Allocated is overstated by this much.

d4f30e63-b0c5-5389-a919-03f9effeb56f.name: MemTier Allocated (GB)
d4f30e63-b0c5-5389-a919-03f9effeb56f.description: Sum of configured memory across the cluster's VMs. The one base figure with no native cluster metric. INCLUDES powered-off VMs and templates, so it is an upper bound -- compare it against Allocated Powered On, which does not.

5e22168f-6b00-5ed2-8331-b81d01605604.name: MemTier Tierable of Used (GB)
5e22168f-6b00-5ed2-8331-b81d01605604.formula: (((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|consumed_average, depth=1}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1})) / 2) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
5e22168f-6b00-5ed2-8331-b81d01605604.description: Cold memory currently backed in DRAM, halved for conservatism. Blank means the active metric is missing, not that everything is cold. Consumed minus active, in that order -- active is the working set within consumed.

a2b1d39f-1ae6-5256-8ba0-d589cad8f611.name: MemTier Active of Allocated (%)
a2b1d39f-1ae6-5256-8ba0-d589cad8f611.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2})) * 100
a2b1d39f-1ae6-5256-8ba0-d589cad8f611.description: Raw active as a share of allocated, with NO headroom factor applied, so the number means what its name says. Apply headroom in the classification, not here.

79b34dab-c8de-569e-8ea5-4e61f24a11a2.name: MemTier Active of Consumed (%)
79b34dab-c8de-569e-8ea5-4e61f24a11a2.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|consumed_average, depth=1})) * 100
79b34dab-c8de-569e-8ea5-4e61f24a11a2.description: Plausibility check on the whole exercise. Typical estates sit at 8-12%, nearer 15% where databases dominate. Outside 5-20% suspect the metric, not the workload.

81b53d69-3fca-5816-a129-c89c6edc39bb.name: MemTier Unused (GB)
81b53d69-3fca-5816-a129-c89c6edc39bb.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|consumed_average, depth=1})) / 1048576
81b53d69-3fca-5816-a129-c89c6edc39bb.description: allocated - consumed. Memory configured to guests that the host has never had to back. Overcommit you are already harvesting, and the cheapest headroom there is.

680c80b8-2936-5438-bb96-f34f7f9d8e65.name: MemTier Unallocated (GB)
680c80b8-2936-5438-bb96-f34f7f9d8e65.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|host_provisioned, depth=1}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2})) / 1048576
680c80b8-2936-5438-bb96-f34f7f9d8e65.description: available - allocated. Installed memory handed to no VM. NEGATIVE MEANS THE CLUSTER IS OVERCOMMITTED, which is a useful signal in itself -- it is deliberately not clamped at zero.

8c5343d0-55c5-5bfc-adae-cda5efeba33f.name: MemTier Active of Host RAM (%)
8c5343d0-55c5-5bfc-adae-cda5efeba33f.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|host_provisioned, depth=1})) * 100
8c5343d0-55c5-5bfc-adae-cda5efeba33f.description: active / available. The working set against the memory actually installed. This is the one that says whether a DRAM tier sized at today's hardware would hold the workload at all.

4ad27278-e166-5e1e-aa59-c10a117694d1.name: MemTier Overcommit (%)
4ad27278-e166-5e1e-aa59-c10a117694d1.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|host_provisioned, depth=1})) * 100
4ad27278-e166-5e1e-aa59-c10a117694d1.description: allocated / available. Under 100% the cluster is not overcommitted. Estates that do overcommit typically sit 5-10% over, so 100-110% is mild and only past 110% is worth flagging -- judged on typical allocation, not on a peak, because allocation is a configuration fact that drifts slowly rather than a spiky metric.

074f9e28-fb57-5bfa-841b-4244a6ba3fa3.name: MemTier Pinned VMs
074f9e28-fb57-5bfa-841b-4244a6ba3fa3.description: Count of VMs pinned to DRAM and therefore untierable, for any reason the adapter can see. Zero is the expected answer; a non-zero count caps what tiering can achieve here no matter how cold the cluster looks.

1cbdf1c7-87e7-575a-a35d-c39c8604f3c6.name: MemTier Pinned Memory (GB)
1cbdf1c7-87e7-575a-a35d-c39c8604f3c6.description: Configured memory belonging to pinned VMs. This much of the cluster must be DRAM regardless of the sizing model -- subtract it before believing any saving.

4e1bb9de-0b09-526d-90f2-fa9437828e9b.name: MemTier Tierable Memory (GB)
4e1bb9de-0b09-526d-90f2-fa9437828e9b.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) / 1048576) - (sum(${adaptertype=MemTierAdvanced, objecttype=MemTierAdvancedVM, metric=pinnedMemoryKB, depth=3}) / 1048576)
4e1bb9de-0b09-526d-90f2-fa9437828e9b.description: Allocated memory minus memory pinned to DRAM: the honest ceiling on what tiering can address in this cluster.

374b9a22-2ab1-5275-8638-3ecc2df62629.name: MemTier RAM Saved at Floor (GB)
374b9a22-2ab1-5275-8638-3ecc2df62629.formula: ((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1})) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
374b9a22-2ab1-5275-8638-3ecc2df62629.description: allocated - peak active. RAM you would NOT have to buy if this cluster were tiered and DRAM sized to the working set. Read with the Maximum transformation over a full business cycle; blank means the active metric is missing.

3222e9d7-fdfa-5723-b6a3-5b84cafb0cdf.name: MemTier RAM Saved Conservative (GB)
3222e9d7-fdfa-5723-b6a3-5b84cafb0cdf.formula: ((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) - (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) * 4.0)) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
3222e9d7-fdfa-5723-b6a3-5b84cafb0cdf.description: allocated - (4 x peak active). The saving with the planning factor applied rather than the floor. Negative means the conservative DRAM figure exceeds what is allocated today, i.e. tiering saves nothing at this factor.

0f9d8553-db55-5dad-85d3-398ddc38807a.name: MemTier Retrofit Headroom (GB)
0f9d8553-db55-5dad-85d3-398ddc38807a.formula: ((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|host_provisioned, depth=1}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1})) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
0f9d8553-db55-5dad-85d3-398ddc38807a.description: Installed DRAM minus peak active. POSITIVE means the working set already fits the DRAM you own, so this cluster can be tiered by adding NVMe alone, with no DRAM purchase. Negative means it cannot, whatever NVMe is added.

b9d812e3-0d77-501e-a8fd-356dc98ba743.name: MemTier Retrofit NVMe to Add (GB)
b9d812e3-0d77-501e-a8fd-356dc98ba743.formula: ((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|host_provisioned, depth=1})) / 1048576)
b9d812e3-0d77-501e-a8fd-356dc98ba743.description: Allocated minus installed DRAM: the NVMe needed to present today's allocated memory on today's hosts. Zero or negative means installed DRAM already covers allocation and tiering would buy capacity you are not yet using.

725d2aa5-8113-5cd0-a446-e488a842e6d2.name: MemTier NVMe per Host (GB)
725d2aa5-8113-5cd0-a446-e488a842e6d2.formula: (((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1})) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=ClusterComputeResource, metric=summary|total_number_hosts, depth=0})
725d2aa5-8113-5cd0-a446-e488a842e6d2.description: NVMe tier each host would carry at the DRAM floor. COMPARE AGAINST 4096 GB: above that the tier exceeds the per-host kernel and partition limit and the design is not buildable, whatever the cluster total says. Reduce the ratio or add hosts.

3801c6bc-164f-531d-90bd-5955463a9779.name: MemTier Active of Allocated at Peak (%)
3801c6bc-164f-531d-90bd-5955463a9779.formula: ((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2})) * 100) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))
3801c6bc-164f-531d-90bd-5955463a9779.description: Peak working set as a share of allocated. The 50% line is the safety limit: above it active memory, not the chosen ratio, is what binds the DRAM size. Below 20% the platform's maximum 1:4 ratio binds instead -- the workload is colder than the platform can exploit.

037a52aa-e1a1-5154-9b74-765c931bf975.name: MemTier CPU Headroom (%)
037a52aa-e1a1-5154-9b74-765c931bf975.formula: 100 - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=cpu|usage_average, depth=1}) / (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=cpu|usage_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=cpu|usage_average, depth=1}))
037a52aa-e1a1-5154-9b74-765c931bf975.description: 100 - CPU utilisation, as a cluster rollup. Compare against Active of Host RAM: the SMALLER headroom is the constraint that binds consolidation first. Tiering only pays where memory binds before CPU. Blank means the CPU metric is missing.

a1343c53-30ca-5c1c-a5e6-0b23dc8429a9.name: MemTier DRAM Required Floor (GB)
a1343c53-30ca-5c1c-a5e6-0b23dc8429a9.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
a1343c53-30ca-5c1c-a5e6-0b23dc8429a9.description: AGGRESSIVE. DRAM sized to the working set and nothing more: at peak, every page the guests are actually touching fits in DRAM and all cold memory lives on NVMe. Blank means the active metric is missing, NOT that no DRAM is needed. This is a floor, not a recommendation -- there is no margin for growth, for a working set that moves, or for active memory being an ESXi estimate rather than a measurement. Read it with the Maximum transformation over 30 days.

e58afed0-71aa-5eb4-aacd-52816d86aa0a.name: MemTier DRAM Required Conservative (GB)
e58afed0-71aa-5eb4-aacd-52816d86aa0a.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) * 4.0 * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
e58afed0-71aa-5eb4-aacd-52816d86aa0a.description: CONSERVATIVE. 4x the working set, so DRAM holds the active set with 4x headroom for growth and for the working set shifting. Starting point for planning, not a final answer -- tune the factor once real peaks are in hand. Read it with the Maximum transformation over 30 days.

8f08be08-04f3-5011-a29c-b4ba4a791ddf.name: MemTier NVMe Required at Floor (GB)
8f08be08-04f3-5011-a29c-b4ba4a791ddf.formula: ((sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2}) - sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1})) * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))) / 1048576
8f08be08-04f3-5011-a29c-b4ba4a791ddf.description: Allocated memory that would sit on NVMe if DRAM were sized to the floor. Negative means the working set already exceeds what is allocated -- investigate before sizing anything on it.

d2f53553-4799-5bfa-9839-d377b6eb64a8.name: MemTier Implied DRAM Share at Floor (%)
d2f53553-4799-5bfa-9839-d377b6eb64a8.formula: (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=VirtualMachine, metric=mem|guest_provisioned, depth=2})) * 100 * (sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}) / sum(${adaptertype=VMWARE, objecttype=HostSystem, metric=mem|active_average, depth=1}))
d2f53553-4799-5bfa-9839-d377b6eb64a8.description: DRAM as a share of presented memory at the floor. Compare against the supported ratios: 50% is 1:1, 33% is 1:2, 20% is 1:4. Below 20% the workload is cold enough that the platform's maximum ratio, not the workload, is the limit.

0b569aec-f244-5e72-9839-70e79e04ee76.name: MemTier Fleet RAM Saved at Floor (GB)
0b569aec-f244-5e72-9839-70e79e04ee76.description: Total RAM not purchased across every cluster tagged into this group. The headline number, and it only counts clusters someone opted in.

89ed6e03-e4f6-5331-843b-576be1c1defe.name: MemTier Fleet RAM Saved Conservative (GB)
89ed6e03-e4f6-5331-843b-576be1c1defe.description: The same total with the planning factor applied rather than the floor.

33aeec80-19f2-5b2d-b711-59675af2c9b6.name: MemTier Fleet Allocated Powered On (GB)
33aeec80-19f2-5b2d-b711-59675af2c9b6.description: Allocated memory across the opted-in clusters, running VMs only.

073c7ab6-352d-5101-a80d-bad4ddef5700.name: MemTier Fleet Pinned Memory (GB)
073c7ab6-352d-5101-a80d-bad4ddef5700.description: Memory across the opted-in clusters that is pinned to DRAM and cannot be tiered. Subtract it from the saving before quoting a number.

420d7b57-1420-5b96-ba32-e7c37459ed2a.name: MemTier TEST Fleet Active depth3 (GB)
420d7b57-1420-5b96-ba32-e7c37459ed2a.description: A/B TEST ONLY. Measured tree depth from vSphere World to HostSystem is 3.

e57c0363-8ca5-5ccc-a660-7595d48b8b87.name: MemTier TEST Fleet Active depth10 (GB)
e57c0363-8ca5-5ccc-a660-7595d48b8b87.description: A/B TEST ONLY. The inherited content uses depth=10. If this one reports data and depth3 does not, depth means 'up to N'; if the reverse, it means 'exactly N'.
